s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of fever and generalized eruption with erythematous plaques, bullae, and target lesions in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face
Several large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
key_facts: 22-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus
Readmitted with fever and a generalized eruption
Temperature of 101.5°F
Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead
Several large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Normocytic anemia with mean corpuscular volume of 99 fL, hemoglobin of 11.7 g/dL, and hematocrit of 33.4%
Thrombocytopenia with platelet count of 81 K/μL
Hypocomplementemia with C3 of 42 mg/dL and C4 of 3 mg/dL
Antinuclear antibody titer of 1:1280 with speckled pattern
Positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with fever, generalized eruption, and target lesions, which are characteristic of Stevens-Johnson syndrome

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and presents with widespread skin lesions and bullae, which are consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis

shortlist.label: Acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and presents with characteristic skin lesions, including erythematous plaques and target lesions

shortlist.label: Bullous systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and presents with bullae and skin lesions, which are consistent with bullous systemic lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with target lesions and a history of autoimmune disease, which are consistent with erythema multiforme

raw.rationale: The presence of fever, generalized eruption, and numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers, along with the biopsy findings of dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes, are consistent with Stevens-Johnson syndrome. The patient's history of systemic lupus erythematosus and the presence of anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies also support this diagnosis, as these conditions can increase the risk of developing Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

rejected.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
rejected.why: While the patient has a generalized eruption and bullae, the presence of target lesions and the biopsy findings are more consistent with Stevens-Johnson syndrome than toxic epidermal necrolysis.

rejected.label: Acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings are more severe than typical acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, and the presence of bullae and target lesions are not typical of this condition.

rejected.label: Bullous systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings do not specifically suggest bullous systemic lupus erythematosus, and this condition is relatively rare.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings are more severe and widespread than typical erythema multiforme, and the presence of bullae and target lesions are not typical of this condition.
